title: secp256k1-ecdlp: deterministic generic control truncated at 2/5 coverage

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the deterministic baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 2/5 = 0.40 using at most 2^128.486389 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. The giant search executes H=ceil(ceil(2r/5)/m) steps with m=2^128, so the covered scalar prefix is at least 2r/5 wide and the success probability is the algorithmic coverage itself; inputs outside that prefix are exhausted to an explicit failure and are not retried, restarted or amplified. Peak memory is at most 2^136.000001 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^128.001176 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or heuristic assumptions. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the same truncated BSGS decomposition on a small additive cyclic group and report the measured recovered fraction against the declared 2/5 coverage floor. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
